legend.amalfi.f0: From Sorrento you look across the Bay of Naples to Mount Vesuvius.
legend.amalfi.f1: The Amalfi Coast has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.
legend.amalfi.f2: In the Middle Ages, Amalfi was the capital of a powerful maritime republic.
legend.amalfi.f3: Amalfi’s cathedral, dedicated to Saint Andrew, stands at the top of a grand staircase.
legend.amalfi.f4: In 1880, the gardens of Villa Rufolo in Ravello inspired Richard Wagner for a scene of his opera Parsifal.
legend.amalfi.f5: The coast’s large, fragrant lemons, the Sfusato Amalfitano, are used to make limoncello.
legend.amalfi.f6: Salerno was home to the Schola Medica Salernitana, one of the first medical schools of medieval Europe.
legend.amalfi.liqueur.e: Limoncello, from the Sfusato Amalfitano lemon.
legend.amalfi.liqueur.q: Which liqueur is made from the coast’s lemons?
legend.amalfi.saint.q: To which saint is Amalfi’s cathedral dedicated?
legend.amalfi.salerno.e: The Schola Medica Salernitana, one of Europe’s first medical schools.
legend.amalfi.salerno.q: What was Salerno famous for in the Middle Ages?
legend.amalfi.unesco.q: Since which year is the Amalfi Coast a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
legend.amalfi.wagner.q: Which town’s gardens inspired Richard Wagner in 1880?
legend.eurostar.f0: St Pancras station opened in 1868; its Victorian Gothic hotel façade is a London icon.
legend.eurostar.f1: Eurostar passenger services started in November 1994.
legend.eurostar.f2: The Channel Tunnel is about 50 km long, with about 38 km under the sea — the longest undersea section of any tunnel in the world.
legend.eurostar.f3: At its deepest the tunnel lies about 75 m below sea level. British and French crews met under the Channel in 1990.
legend.eurostar.f4: Paris Gare du Nord is the busiest railway station in Europe by number of passengers.
legend.eurostar.meet.q: In which year did the British and French tunnelling crews meet?
legend.eurostar.pancras.q: When did London St Pancras station open?
legend.eurostar.paris.e: Gare du Nord, the busiest station in Europe.
legend.eurostar.paris.q: At which Paris station does Eurostar arrive?
legend.eurostar.start.q: When did Eurostar passenger services start?
legend.eurostar.undersea.e: About 38 km of its roughly 50 km.
legend.eurostar.undersea.q: About how much of the Channel Tunnel is under the sea?
legend.glacier.f0: The Glacier Express has run between Zermatt and St. Moritz since 1930.
legend.glacier.f1: It is nicknamed “the slowest express train in the world”: the whole trip takes about 8 hours.
legend.glacier.f2: Its highest point is the Oberalp Pass, at 2,033 m.
legend.glacier.f3: Along the way the train crosses 291 bridges and goes through 91 tunnels.
legend.glacier.f4: Chur is often described as the oldest town in Switzerland.
legend.glacier.f5: After Chur the train takes the Albula line, part of the Rhaetian Railway UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008.
legend.glacier.f6: On the Albula line, the 65 m-high Landwasser Viaduct sends the train straight into a tunnel in the cliff.
legend.glacier.nick.e: The slowest express train in the world: about 8 hours.
legend.glacier.nick.o0: The slowest express train in the world
legend.glacier.nick.o2: The oldest train in the Alps
legend.glacier.nick.q: What is the Glacier Express nicknamed?
legend.glacier.pass.q: What is the highest point of the Glacier Express?
legend.glacier.since.q: Since which year has the Glacier Express run?
legend.glacier.unesco.e: Since 2008 (Rhaetian Railway in the Albula / Bernina Landscapes).
legend.glacier.unesco.q: Since when is the Albula line part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
legend.glacier.viaduct.q: Which viaduct sends the train straight into a tunnel in a cliff?
legend.greatoceanroad.built.e: Returned soldiers, between 1919 and 1932: it is a war memorial.
legend.greatoceanroad.built.q: Who built the Great Ocean Road?
legend.greatoceanroad.capital.e: Until 1927, when Parliament moved to Canberra.
legend.greatoceanroad.capital.q: Until which year was Melbourne the seat of Australia’s federal government?
legend.greatoceanroad.f0: Melbourne was the seat of Australia’s federal government from 1901 to 1927, before Canberra.
legend.greatoceanroad.f1: The Great Ocean Road starts near Torquay, home of the famous Bells Beach surf contest.
legend.greatoceanroad.f2: Returned soldiers built the road between 1919 and 1932 in memory of those killed in the First World War: it is the world’s largest war memorial.
legend.greatoceanroad.f3: Around Kennett River and Cape Otway, wild koalas are often seen in the trees.
legend.greatoceanroad.f4: The Twelve Apostles are limestone stacks carved by the Southern Ocean; despite the name, fewer than twelve stand today.
legend.greatoceanroad.f5: From June to September, southern right whales often come to calve near Warrnambool.
legend.greatoceanroad.rock.e: Limestone, carved by the Southern Ocean.
legend.greatoceanroad.rock.q: What are the Twelve Apostles made of?
legend.greatoceanroad.surf.e: Bells Beach, home of a famous surf contest.
legend.greatoceanroad.surf.q: Which famous surf beach is near Torquay?
legend.greatoceanroad.whales.e: Southern right whales, from June to September.
legend.greatoceanroad.whales.q: Which whales come to calve near Warrnambool?
legend.home.sub: Ten mythic routes with stories told at each stop, special questions and local phrases.
legend.home.title: 🌟 Legendary journeys
legend.med-cruise.f0: Several works by Antoni Gaudí in Barcelona, such as Park Güell, are UNESCO World Heritage.
legend.med-cruise.f1: Marseille, France’s oldest city, was founded around 600 BC by Greek sailors from Phocaea, as Massalia.
legend.med-cruise.f2: Genoa is widely considered the birthplace of Christopher Columbus.
legend.med-cruise.f3: Civitavecchia, Rome’s cruise port, was developed as a harbour by Emperor Trajan in the early 2nd century.
legend.med-cruise.f4: Naples lies beneath Mount Vesuvius, whose eruption in 79 AD buried Pompeii.
legend.med-cruise.f5: Palma’s Gothic cathedral, La Seu, stands right above the sea.
legend.med-cruise.genoa.q: Which explorer is widely considered to be from Genoa?
legend.med-cruise.massalia.e: Greek sailors from Phocaea, who named it Massalia.
legend.med-cruise.trajan.q: Which emperor developed the harbour of Civitavecchia?
legend.med-cruise.volcano.e: Mount Vesuvius, which buried Pompeii in 79 AD.
legend.norway.alesund.q: In which style was Ålesund rebuilt after the 1904 fire?
legend.norway.bryggen.q: In which city is the Bryggen wharf?
legend.norway.f0: Near Stavanger, Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock) towers about 604 m above the Lysefjord.
legend.norway.f1: Bergen’s Bryggen wharf, with its colourful Hanseatic wooden houses, has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.
legend.norway.f2: Flåm lies on a branch of the Sognefjord, Norway’s longest and deepest fjord (about 205 km long and up to 1,308 m deep).
legend.norway.f3: The Flåm Railway climbs about 863 m in about 20 km, one of the steepest standard-gauge lines in the world.
legend.norway.f4: The Geirangerfjord and the Nærøyfjord have been UNESCO World Heritage together since 2005.
legend.norway.f5: Opposite the Seven Sisters waterfall stands another fall nicknamed “the Suitor”.
legend.norway.f6: Ålesund was rebuilt in Art Nouveau style after a fire destroyed the town in 1904.
legend.norway.pulpit.q: Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock) towers above which fjord?
legend.norway.unesco.q: Since which year are the Geirangerfjord and Nærøyfjord UNESCO World Heritage?
legend.pch.aquarium.e: A sardine cannery on Cannery Row, in 1984.
legend.pch.aquarium.q: The Monterey Bay Aquarium opened in a former…
legend.pch.bixby.q: Which Big Sur bridge, opened in 1932, is one of California’s most photographed?
legend.pch.f0: Most of this drive follows California State Route 1, which runs along much of the state’s Pacific coast.
legend.pch.f1: The Monterey Bay Aquarium opened in 1984 in a former sardine cannery on Cannery Row.
legend.pch.f2: Bixby Creek Bridge, one of the most photographed bridges in California, opened in 1932.
legend.pch.f3: At Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park, McWay Falls (about 24 m high) pours onto a beach at the edge of the Pacific.
legend.pch.f4: North of San Luis Obispo, at San Simeon, Hearst Castle was built for newspaper publisher William Randolph Hearst between 1919 and 1947.
legend.pch.f5: Mission Santa Barbara, founded in 1786, is nicknamed the “Queen of the Missions”.
legend.pch.f6: Los Angeles is the second most populous city in the United States.
legend.pch.hearst.e: William Randolph Hearst; it was built between 1919 and 1947.
legend.pch.hearst.q: Hearst Castle was built for which newspaper publisher?
legend.pch.mission.q: Which mission is nicknamed the “Queen of the Missions”?
legend.pch.route.q: Which road follows much of California’s Pacific coast?
legend.route66.author.e: John Steinbeck, in The Grapes of Wrath (1939).
legend.route66.author.q: Which author called Route 66 “the Mother Road”?
legend.route66.end.e: Santa Monica, where a sign on the pier marks the “End of the Trail”.
legend.route66.end.q: Where is the traditional western end of Route 66?
legend.route66.f0: Route 66 was commissioned in 1926 and linked Chicago to Santa Monica: about 3,940 km (2,448 miles).
legend.route66.f1: John Steinbeck nicknamed it “the Mother Road” in his 1939 novel The Grapes of Wrath.
legend.route66.f2: The road crossed eight states — Illinois, Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and California — with only about 13 miles in Kansas.
legend.route66.f3: Tulsa businessman Cyrus Avery is often called the “Father of Route 66” for his role in creating it.
legend.route66.f4: Near Amarillo, the Cadillac Ranch art installation (1974) shows ten Cadillacs buried nose-first in a field.
legend.route66.f5: The 1946 song “(Get Your Kicks on) Route 66”, written by Bobby Troup, made the road famous around the world.
legend.route66.f6: Route 66 was removed from the US Highway System in 1985, replaced by Interstate highways.
legend.route66.f7: A sign on the Santa Monica Pier marks the symbolic “End of the Trail”.
legend.route66.removed.e: In 1985, after the Interstate highways replaced it.
legend.route66.removed.q: In which year was Route 66 removed from the US Highway System?
legend.route66.states.e: Eight: Illinois, Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Texas, New Mexico, Arizona and California.
legend.route66.states.q: How many US states did Route 66 cross?
legend.route66.year.q: In which year was Route 66 commissioned?
legend.tokaido.f0: The Tōkaidō Shinkansen opened on 1 October 1964, just before the Tokyo Olympic Games.
legend.tokaido.f1: “Shinkansen” means “new trunk line”. The Tōkaidō was the old road linking Edo (Tokyo) with Kyoto.
legend.tokaido.f2: Heading towards Osaka, Mount Fuji appears on the right-hand side of the train (seats E on most trains), weather permitting.
legend.tokaido.f3: Nagoya is the heart of Japan’s car industry: Toyota has its headquarters nearby.
legend.tokaido.f4: Kyoto was Japan’s imperial capital for more than a thousand years, from 794 to 1868.
legend.tokaido.f5: The fastest Nozomi trains link Tokyo and Shin-Osaka in about two and a half hours.
legend.tokaido.fuji.e: On the right-hand side (seats E), weather permitting.
legend.tokaido.fuji.q: Travelling from Tokyo to Osaka, on which side do you see Mount Fuji?
legend.tokaido.kyoto.q: From which year was Kyoto Japan’s imperial capital?
legend.tokaido.open.q: In which year did the Tōkaidō Shinkansen open?
legend.tokaido.road.e: The old “Eastern Sea Road” between Edo (Tokyo) and Kyoto.
legend.tokaido.road.o0: A road between Edo and Kyoto
legend.transsib.built.e: In 1891; the main line was completed in 1916.
legend.transsib.built.q: In which year did construction of the Trans-Siberian begin?
legend.transsib.f0: The Trans-Siberian Railway is about 9,289 km long — the longest railway line in the world.
legend.transsib.f1: Construction began in 1891 and the main line was completed in 1916.
legend.transsib.f2: Near Yekaterinburg, the line crosses the symbolic border between Europe and Asia.
legend.transsib.f3: Novosibirsk, Russia’s third-largest city, was founded in 1893 where the railway crossed the Ob River.
legend.transsib.f4: After Irkutsk the line follows the southern shore of Lake Baikal, the deepest lake in the world.
legend.transsib.f5: Ulan-Ude, capital of Buryatia, has a giant head of Lenin often said to be the largest in the world.
legend.transsib.f6: At Khabarovsk the railway crosses the wide Amur River.
legend.transsib.f7: Moscow is on UTC+3 and Vladivostok on UTC+10: a 7-hour time difference. The name Vladivostok means roughly “Ruler of the East”.
legend.transsib.lake.e: Lake Baikal, the deepest lake in the world.
legend.transsib.lake.q: Which lake does the line run along after Irkutsk?
legend.transsib.length.e: About 9,289 km, the longest railway line in the world.
legend.transsib.length.q: About how long is the Trans-Siberian Railway?
legend.transsib.name.q: What does the name “Vladivostok” roughly mean?
legend.transsib.tz.e: 7 hours: UTC+3 in Moscow, UTC+10 in Vladivostok.
legend.transsib.tz.q: What is the time difference between Moscow and Vladivostok?
lm.abusimbel.clue: Rock temples of Ramesses II that were moved block by block in the 1960s to escape a rising reservoir.
lm.abusimbel.fact: Rock temples built for Ramesses II; between 1964 and 1968 they were cut into blocks and moved to escape the rising waters of Lake Nasser.
lm.abusimbel.name: Abu Simbel temples
lm.alhambra.clue: A palace-fortress built largely by the Nasrid dynasty, famous for its courtyards and intricate stucco.
lm.alhambra.fact: A palace and fortress complex largely built by the Nasrid dynasty, the last Muslim dynasty of the Iberian Peninsula.
lm.alhambra.name: Alhambra
lm.angkor.clue: A huge 12th-century temple complex, originally Hindu, that appears on its country’s national flag.
lm.angkor.fact: Built in the early 12th century under King Suryavarman II, originally dedicated to Vishnu; it appears on the national flag.
lm.angkor.name: Angkor Wat
lm.atomium.clue: A building shaped like an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times, built for Expo 58.
lm.atomium.fact: Built for the 1958 Brussels World’s Fair (Expo 58), it represents an iron crystal magnified 165 billion times.
lm.atomium.name: Atomium
lm.bagan.clue: An ancient city where more than 2,000 Buddhist temples and pagodas dot the plains.
lm.bagan.fact: An ancient city where more than 2,000 Buddhist temples and pagodas still stand on the plains.
lm.bagan.name: Bagan
lm.bigben.clue: A clock tower at the north end of a parliament building; its famous nickname actually belongs to the great bell.
lm.bigben.fact: “Big Ben” is strictly the nickname of the great bell; the clock tower was renamed Elizabeth Tower in 2012.
lm.bigben.name: Big Ben (Elizabeth Tower)
lm.bluemosque.clue: A mosque completed in 1616 with six minarets, nicknamed for the colour of its tiles.
lm.bluemosque.fact: Completed in 1616; nicknamed the Blue Mosque for its blue İznik tiles. It has six minarets.
lm.bluemosque.name: Sultan Ahmed Mosque (Blue Mosque)
lm.borobudur.clue: The largest Buddhist temple in the world, built in the 9th century with hundreds of stupas.
lm.borobudur.fact: A 9th-century Mahayana Buddhist temple and the largest Buddhist temple in the world.
lm.borobudur.name: Borobudur
lm.brandenburg.clue: A neoclassical gate completed in 1791 and topped by a four-horse chariot sculpture.
lm.brandenburg.fact: A neoclassical gate completed in 1791, topped by the Quadriga — a chariot drawn by four horses.
lm.brandenburg.name: Brandenburg Gate
lm.burj.clue: A 828-metre skyscraper that opened in 2010 and became the tallest building in the world.
lm.burj.fact: At 828 m, it has been the world’s tallest building since it opened in 2010.
lm.burj.name: Burj Khalifa
lm.charlesbridge.clue: A medieval stone bridge lined with statues, begun in 1357 under King Charles IV.
lm.charlesbridge.fact: A medieval stone bridge over the Vltava, begun in 1357 under King Charles IV.
lm.charlesbridge.name: Charles Bridge
lm.chichen.clue: A pre-Columbian Maya city whose step pyramid honours a feathered serpent deity.
lm.chichen.fact: A large pre-Columbian Maya city whose step pyramid, El Castillo, is dedicated to the feathered serpent deity Kukulcán.
lm.chichen.name: Chichén Itzá
lm.cntower.clue: A 553-metre concrete communications tower completed in 1976 on the shore of a Great Lake.
lm.cntower.fact: A 553.3 m concrete communications tower completed in 1976.
lm.cntower.name: CN Tower
lm.colosseum.clue: The largest amphitheatre ever built in antiquity, completed in 80 AD and used for gladiator contests.
lm.colosseum.fact: Completed in 80 AD under Emperor Titus, it is the largest ancient amphitheatre ever built.
lm.colosseum.name: Colosseum
lm.cristo.clue: An Art Deco statue with outstretched arms, completed in 1931 on top of a mountain overlooking a bay.
lm.cristo.fact: An Art Deco statue completed in 1931 on top of Corcovado mountain.
lm.cristo.name: Christ the Redeemer
lm.djenne.clue: The largest mud-brick building in the world, re-plastered by the community every year.
lm.djenne.fact: The largest mud-brick building in the world; the current structure dates from 1907.
lm.djenne.name: Great Mosque of Djenné
lm.dubrovnik.clue: Stone defensive walls almost 2 km long encircling an old town on the Adriatic.
lm.dubrovnik.fact: Defensive stone walls nearly 2 km long encircling the old town on the Adriatic coast.
lm.dubrovnik.name: Walls of Dubrovnik
lm.duomo.clue: A cathedral whose enormous brick dome was engineered by Brunelleschi in the 15th century.
lm.duomo.fact: Its huge brick dome was engineered by Filippo Brunelleschi in the 15th century.
lm.duomo.name: Florence Cathedral (Il Duomo)
lm.edinburghcastle.clue: A fortress built on the rocky plug of an extinct volcano above a capital city.
lm.edinburghcastle.fact: A fortress on Castle Rock, the plug of an extinct volcano.
lm.edinburghcastle.name: Edinburgh Castle
lm.eiffel.clue: A wrought-iron lattice tower completed in 1889 for a World’s Fair, once criticised by artists and now a national symbol.
lm.eiffel.fact: Completed in 1889 as the entrance arch of the Exposition Universelle (World’s Fair).
lm.eiffel.name: Eiffel Tower
lm.everest.clue: Earth’s highest mountain above sea level, re-measured in 2020 at 8,848.86 m.
lm.everest.fact: Earth’s highest mountain above sea level: 8,848.86 m, per the 2020 survey by China and Nepal.
lm.everest.name: Mount Everest
lm.forbiddencity.clue: An imperial palace built from 1406 to 1420, home to emperors of two dynasties and now a museum.
lm.forbiddencity.fact: The imperial palace of the Ming and Qing dynasties, built from 1406 to 1420; today it houses the Palace Museum.
lm.forbiddencity.name: Forbidden City
lm.fuji.clue: Its country’s highest mountain at 3,776 m — an active volcano that last erupted in 1707.
lm.fuji.fact: At 3,776 m it is the highest mountain in Japan; this active volcano last erupted in 1707.
lm.fuji.name: Mount Fuji
lm.fushimi.clue: A Shinto shrine with thousands of vermilion gates lining the trails up a mountain.
lm.fushimi.fact: A Shinto shrine famous for thousands of vermilion torii gates lining trails up Mount Inari.
lm.fushimi.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
lm.gatewayarch.clue: The world’s tallest arch at 192 m, a stainless-steel monument completed in 1965.
lm.gatewayarch.fact: At 192 m, completed in 1965, it is the world’s tallest arch.
lm.gatewayarch.name: Gateway Arch
lm.giza.clue: The only Wonder of the Ancient World still largely standing, built around 2560 BC for a pharaoh.
lm.giza.fact: Built around 2560 BC for the pharaoh Khufu; it is the oldest of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and the only one largely intact.
lm.giza.name: Great Pyramid of Giza
lm.goldengate.clue: A suspension bridge opened in 1937, painted in a colour officially called “International Orange”.
lm.goldengate.fact: Opened in 1937; its famous colour is called “International Orange”.
lm.goldengate.name: Golden Gate Bridge
lm.grandcanyon.clue: A steep-sided canyon carved over millions of years by the Colorado River.
lm.grandcanyon.fact: A steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River.
lm.grandcanyon.name: Grand Canyon
lm.greatwall.clue: A series of fortifications built over many centuries; its best-preserved sections date from the Ming dynasty.
lm.greatwall.fact: A series of fortifications built over many centuries; most of the well-preserved sections, like Badaling, date from the Ming dynasty.
lm.greatwall.name: Great Wall of China (Badaling)
lm.gyeongbokgung.clue: The main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, first built in 1395.
lm.gyeongbokgung.fact: The main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, first built in 1395.
lm.gyeongbokgung.name: Gyeongbokgung
lm.hagiasophia.clue: A domed building completed in 537 under Emperor Justinian I.
lm.hagiasophia.fact: Completed in 537 under the Byzantine emperor Justinian I, its huge dome was an engineering marvel.
lm.hagiasophia.name: Hagia Sophia
lm.halong.clue: A bay dotted with around 1,600 limestone islands and islets.
lm.halong.fact: A bay with around 1,600 limestone islands and islets.
lm.halong.name: Hạ Long Bay
lm.harbourbridge.clue: A steel arch bridge opened in 1932, affectionately nicknamed “the Coathanger”.
lm.harbourbridge.fact: A steel arch bridge opened in 1932, nicknamed “the Coathanger”.
lm.harbourbridge.name: Sydney Harbour Bridge
lm.iguazu.clue: A huge system of waterfalls on the border between Argentina and Brazil.
lm.iguazu.fact: Hundreds of individual waterfalls on the Iguazú River, on the border between Argentina and Brazil.
lm.iguazu.name: Iguazú Falls
lm.kilimanjaro.clue: The highest mountain of its continent at 5,895 m, a dormant volcano near the equator.
lm.kilimanjaro.fact: At 5,895 m it is the highest mountain in Africa and the highest free-standing mountain in the world.
lm.kilimanjaro.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
lm.kinkakuji.clue: A Zen temple whose top two floors are covered in gold leaf, reflected in a pond.
lm.kinkakuji.fact: A Zen Buddhist temple whose top two floors are covered in gold leaf.
lm.kinkakuji.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
lm.lalibela.clue: Eleven medieval churches carved downward out of solid rock.
lm.lalibela.fact: Eleven medieval monolithic churches carved downward out of solid rock.
lm.lalibela.name: Rock-hewn churches of Lalibela
lm.liberty.clue: A copper statue dedicated in 1886, a gift from France, holding a torch above a harbour.
lm.liberty.fact: A gift from the people of France, dedicated in 1886. Gustave Eiffel’s company designed its internal iron framework.
lm.liberty.name: Statue of Liberty
lm.louvre.clue: A glass-and-metal pyramid completed in 1989 as the entrance of the world’s most-visited art museum.
lm.louvre.fact: The glass-and-metal pyramid designed by I. M. Pei was completed in 1989 as the main entrance of the Louvre museum.
lm.louvre.name: Louvre Pyramid
lm.machupicchu.clue: A 15th-century Inca citadel perched on a mountain ridge, internationally publicised in 1911.
lm.machupicchu.fact: A 15th-century Inca citadel on a mountain ridge above the Urubamba valley, brought to international attention in 1911 by Hiram Bingham.
lm.machupicchu.name: Machu Picchu
lm.matterhorn.clue: A 4,478 m pyramid-shaped Alpine peak on the Swiss–Italian border.
lm.matterhorn.fact: A 4,478 m pyramid-shaped peak on the border between Switzerland and Italy.
lm.matterhorn.name: Matterhorn
lm.meteora.clue: Orthodox monasteries perched on top of huge natural rock pillars.
lm.meteora.fact: Eastern Orthodox monasteries built on top of huge natural rock pillars.
lm.meteora.name: Meteora
lm.milford.clue: A fiord with sheer cliffs and waterfalls in a southern national park.
lm.milford.fact: A fiord in Fiordland National Park on the South Island.
lm.milford.name: Milford Sound
lm.moai.clue: Giant monolithic human figures carved from volcanic tuff on a remote Pacific island.
lm.moai.fact: Monolithic human figures carved by the Rapa Nui people, most from volcanic tuff quarried at Rano Raraku.
lm.moai.name: Moai of Rapa Nui
lm.moher.clue: Dramatic sea cliffs about 214 m high facing the Atlantic Ocean.
lm.moher.fact: Sea cliffs on the Atlantic coast rising to about 214 m.
lm.moher.name: Cliffs of Moher
lm.montsaintmichel.clue: A tidal island crowned by a medieval abbey, sometimes surrounded by the sea at high tide.
lm.montsaintmichel.fact: A tidal island crowned by an abbey; at high tide it can be surrounded by the sea.
lm.montsaintmichel.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
lm.neuschwanstein.clue: A 19th-century hilltop palace commissioned by a Bavarian king, begun in 1869.
lm.neuschwanstein.fact: A 19th-century palace commissioned by King Ludwig II of Bavaria; construction began in 1869.
lm.neuschwanstein.name: Neuschwanstein Castle
lm.niagara.clue: Three waterfalls straddling the border between two North American countries.
lm.niagara.fact: Three waterfalls straddling the border between Canada and the United States.
lm.niagara.name: Niagara Falls
lm.operahouse.clue: A performing-arts centre with sail-like shells, designed by a Danish architect and opened in 1973.
lm.operahouse.fact: Designed by Danish architect Jørn Utzon and opened in 1973; a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2007.
lm.operahouse.name: Sydney Opera House
lm.pamukkale.clue: White travertine terraces formed by hot springs; the name means “cotton castle”.
lm.pamukkale.fact: White travertine terraces formed by mineral-rich hot springs; the name means “cotton castle”.
lm.pamukkale.name: Pamukkale
lm.parthenon.clue: A 5th-century BC temple dedicated to the goddess Athena, standing on a rocky hill above the city.
lm.parthenon.fact: A temple on the Acropolis dedicated to the goddess Athena, built in the 5th century BC.
lm.parthenon.name: Parthenon
lm.peritomoreno.clue: A Patagonian glacier famous for huge ice blocks crashing into a lake.
lm.peritomoreno.fact: A glacier in Los Glaciares National Park, famous for ice blocks crashing into Lake Argentino.
lm.peritomoreno.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
lm.petra.clue: An ancient Nabataean city whose façades are carved directly into rose-coloured sandstone cliffs.
lm.petra.fact: The Nabataean capital, famous for buildings carved directly into rose-coloured sandstone cliffs.
lm.petra.name: Petra
lm.petronas.clue: Twin 452 m skyscrapers linked by a sky bridge, the world’s tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.
lm.petronas.fact: Twin 452 m skyscrapers that were the tallest buildings in the world from 1998 to 2004.
lm.petronas.name: Petronas Towers
lm.pisa.clue: A cathedral bell tower begun in 1173 that started tilting during construction because of soft ground.
lm.pisa.fact: The bell tower of Pisa Cathedral; construction began in 1173 and the tilt started during construction because of soft ground.
lm.pisa.name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
lm.sagrada.clue: A basilica begun in 1882 and shaped by a Catalan architect who worked on it until his death in 1926.
lm.sagrada.fact: Construction began in 1882; Antoni Gaudí took over the project in 1883 and worked on it until his death in 1926.
lm.sagrada.name: Sagrada Família
lm.schonbrunn.clue: A Baroque palace that served as the main summer residence of the Habsburg rulers.
lm.schonbrunn.fact: The main summer residence of the Habsburg rulers.
lm.schonbrunn.name: Schönbrunn Palace
lm.spaceneedle.clue: A flying-saucer-topped observation tower built for the 1962 World’s Fair.
lm.spaceneedle.fact: An observation tower built for the 1962 World’s Fair.
lm.spaceneedle.name: Space Needle
lm.stbasil.clue: A church with colourful onion domes built from 1555 to 1561 on the orders of Ivan the Terrible.
lm.stbasil.fact: Built from 1555 to 1561 on the orders of Ivan the Terrible, famous for its colourful onion domes.
lm.stbasil.name: Saint Basil’s Cathedral
lm.stonehenge.clue: A prehistoric ring of standing stones built in stages between roughly 3000 and 2000 BC.
lm.stonehenge.fact: A prehistoric monument built in several stages, roughly between 3000 BC and 2000 BC.
lm.stonehenge.name: Stonehenge
lm.stpeters.clue: A Renaissance basilica in the world’s smallest country, with a dome designed by Michelangelo.
lm.stpeters.fact: A Renaissance church whose dome was designed by Michelangelo.
lm.stpeters.name: St. Peter’s Basilica
lm.sugarloaf.clue: A granite peak at the mouth of a bay, reached by cable car.
lm.sugarloaf.fact: A granite peak at the mouth of Guanabara Bay, reached by cable car.
lm.sugarloaf.name: Sugarloaf Mountain
lm.tablemountain.clue: A flat-topped mountain whose summit cloud is nicknamed the “tablecloth”.
lm.tablemountain.fact: A flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town; its summit is often covered by a cloud nicknamed the “tablecloth”.
lm.tablemountain.name: Table Mountain
lm.taj.clue: A white-marble mausoleum on a river bank, commissioned in 1632 by an emperor for his beloved wife.
lm.taj.fact: Commissioned in 1632 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
lm.taj.name: Taj Mahal
lm.teotihuacan.clue: An ancient Mesoamerican city with a Pyramid of the Sun and an “Avenue of the Dead”.
lm.teotihuacan.fact: An ancient Mesoamerican city known for the Pyramid of the Sun and the Avenue of the Dead.
lm.teotihuacan.name: Teotihuacan
lm.tikal.clue: One of the largest ancient Maya cities, its temples rising above a rainforest canopy.
lm.tikal.fact: One of the largest ancient Maya cities, its temples rise above the rainforest canopy.
lm.tikal.name: Tikal
lm.towerbridge.clue: A bascule and suspension bridge with two towers, opened in 1894 over a famous river.
lm.towerbridge.fact: A combined bascule and suspension bridge over the Thames, opened in 1894.
lm.towerbridge.name: Tower Bridge
lm.uluru.clue: A huge sandstone monolith in a desert, sacred to its Aboriginal custodians; climbing has been banned since 2019.
lm.uluru.fact: A large sandstone formation sacred to the Aṉangu, the Aboriginal people of the area. Climbing it has been banned since 2019.
lm.uluru.name: Uluru
lm.uyuni.clue: The world’s largest salt flat, which becomes a giant mirror after rain.
lm.uyuni.fact: The world’s largest salt flat, over 10,000 km².
lm.uyuni.name: Salar de Uyuni
lm.versailles.clue: A royal palace famous for its Hall of Mirrors, where a 1919 peace treaty was signed.
lm.versailles.fact: The royal residence of Louis XIV, famous for its Hall of Mirrors, where the Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.
lm.versailles.name: Palace of Versailles
lm.victoriafalls.clue: A waterfall on the Zambezi whose local name means “The Smoke That Thunders”.
lm.victoriafalls.fact: A waterfall on the Zambezi River, locally known as Mosi-oa-Tunya, “The Smoke That Thunders”.
lm.victoriafalls.name: Victoria Falls
lm.watarun.clue: The “Temple of Dawn”, decorated with porcelain, on the bank of a great river.
lm.watarun.fact: The “Temple of Dawn” on the west bank of the Chao Phraya River.
lm.watarun.name: Wat Arun
lm.zayed.clue: A vast white-marble mosque completed in 2007 in a Gulf capital city.
lm.zayed.fact: Completed in 2007, it is one of the largest mosques in the world.
lm.zayed.name: Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
lock.audio: 🔊 The audio guide keeps telling you about the places you pass — no need to touch the screen.
lock.enableGps: 🛰️ Turn on the GPS safety lock
lock.intro: You told me you are the driver. Turn on GPS so I can unlock automatically when you are stopped — or confirm you are safely parked.
lock.moving: The vehicle is moving. The game is locked for the driver until you stop.
lock.tip: Tip: hand the phone to a passenger — they can play the whole trip.
lock.title: Eyes on the road!
lock.waitingGps: Waiting for a GPS fix… I unlock automatically once I can see you are stopped.

lookup.failed: Lookup failed. Enter the details manually.

map.listMode: Can’t tap the map? Choose from a list
map.noWebgl: This device cannot display the interactive map (WebGL unavailable). Quizzes and trips still work.
map.youTapped: You tapped {tapped}. {target} is highlighted in gold.
mascot.correct.0: Correct! I would have said the same thing. Slightly faster.
mascot.correct.1: Magnificent! Even my hat is impressed.
mascot.correct.2: Yes! You are officially less lost than yesterday.
mascot.correct.3: Bravo! Put that on a postcard.
mascot.correct.4: Right answer! My binoculars saw it coming.
mascot.correct.5: Spot on. I’m adding you to my list of favourite travellers.
mascot.correct.6: Excellent! You navigate like a pigeon with a GPS.
mascot.driver.0: Eyes on the road! I’ll wait for the next stop.
mascot.driver.1: Driver detected: the quiz is parked until you stop. Safety first, trivia second.
mascot.idle.0: Did you know? I know a lot of things. Ask me with a quiz!
mascot.idle.1: Looking out of the window counts as research.
mascot.idle.2: Tip: download your trip before leaving — I work offline too.
mascot.idle.3: A good traveller always has snacks and a quiz ready.
mascot.landing.0: We have arrived! Please collect your luggage and your new facts.
mascot.landing.1: Journey complete! Another dot on your map.
mascot.landing.2: Touchdown! Applause is optional but appreciated.
mascot.levelup.0: LEVEL UP! I’m almost starting to feel threatened.
mascot.levelup.1: Promotion! Your passport just got heavier.
mascot.levelup.2: New level! Somewhere, a map is applauding.
mascot.offline.0: No signal? No problem. I packed everything in my backpack.
mascot.offline.1: Offline mode: my favourite. No one can google the answers.
mascot.perfect.0: A perfect round! I’m framing this one.
mascot.perfect.1: Flawless! I may have to retire. Just kidding, never.
mascot.streak.0: Streak alert! Are you secretly a geography satellite?
mascot.streak.1: Another one! Shall I hand you my hat?
mascot.streak.2: On fire! Careful, the cabin crew will need an extinguisher.
mascot.surprise.0: SURPRISE CHALLENGE! Double XP — no pressure. Some pressure.
mascot.surprise.1: Supreme challenge incoming! Answer this and I’ll double your points.
mascot.takeoff.0: Wheels up! Let’s see what’s down there.
mascot.takeoff.1: Next stop: knowledge. Then the actual destination.
mascot.takeoff.2: Off we go! Window seat recommended.
mascot.timeout.0: Time’s up! The clock is the only guide faster than me.
mascot.timeout.1: Tick tock… too late! Next one, quick!
mascot.welcome.0: Welcome aboard! Your captain knows everything. Almost.
mascot.welcome.1: Ah, a new traveller! Stay close — I have never been lost. Recently.
mascot.welcome.2: Fasten your curiosity. We depart for knowledge in three… two…
mascot.welcome.3: Bonjour, hola, shalom, hello! I speak many languages. Mostly “tourist”.
mascot.welcome.4: The world is big. Luckily, so is my brain.
mascot.wrong.0: Wrong answer! Even my suitcase knew that one.
mascot.wrong.1: Not quite. Don’t worry — I once took a train to the wrong Paris.
mascot.wrong.2: Oops! Happens to the best of us. Rarely to me, but still.
mascot.wrong.3: Close-ish! On a world map, anyway.
mascot.wrong.4: Nope! But now you know — and knowing is half the journey.
mascot.wrong.5: Hmm. Let’s pretend the turbulence made you click that.

play.leaderboardHelp: Add family members in your profile. Online leaderboards are planned as an opt-in feature.

profile.eraseConfirm: Erase ALL players, trips and progress on this device?
profile.familyHelp: Several players can share this device. Each has their own XP, passport, badges and language. Everything stays on this device.
profile.installHelp: To install: on iPhone use Share → “Add to Home Screen”; on Android or desktop use the browser menu → “Install app”.

profile.privacy1: No account, no tracking, no ads, no analytics.
profile.privacy2: Progress, trips and family profiles are stored only on this device.
profile.privacy3: GPS is off by default, used only when you switch it on, and never leaves your device.
profile.privacy4: Online features call public services directly: OpenFreeMap (detailed map), Wikipedia (place cards), OpenStreetMap Nominatim and OSRM (search and routes).

q.c-diadelosmuertos.e: Celebrated on 1–2 November, it honours deceased loved ones with altars (ofrendas).
q.c-diadelosmuertos.q: The Day of the Dead (Día de Muertos) is a famous tradition of which country?
q.c-flamenco.e: Flamenco developed in Andalusia, southern Spain, and is on UNESCO’s intangible heritage list.
q.c-flamenco.q: Flamenco is a traditional art form from which country?
q.c-galapagos.e: The Galápagos are a province of Ecuador, about 900 km off its coast.
q.c-galapagos.q: The Galápagos Islands, which inspired Darwin, belong to which country?
q.c-haka.e: The haka is a Māori ceremonial dance from New Zealand, famously performed by the All Blacks.
q.c-haka.q: The haka is a ceremonial dance of which people?
q.c-hanami.e: Hanami is the custom of enjoying the beauty of flowers, especially cherry blossoms (sakura).
q.c-holi.e: Holi is a Hindu festival celebrated especially in India and Nepal, marking the arrival of spring.
q.c-holi.q: Holi, the “festival of colours”, is mainly celebrated in which country?
q.c-japan-sun.e: The Japanese name Nihon/Nippon literally means “origin of the sun”.
q.c-japan-sun.q: Which country is often called “the Land of the Rising Sun”?
q.c-kangaroo.e: Kangaroos are marsupials found naturally only in Australia (and tree-kangaroos in New Guinea).
q.c-kangaroo.q: Kangaroos are native to which country?
q.c-lemur.e: Lemurs evolved in isolation on Madagascar and live nowhere else in the wild.
q.c-lemur.q: Wild lemurs are found naturally on only one island nation. Which?
q.c-olympics.e: The ancient Games were held at the sanctuary of Zeus in Olympia from 776 BC.
q.c-olympics.q: Where were the ancient Olympic Games held?
q.c-panda.e: Wild giant pandas live in mountain ranges of central China, mainly Sichuan.
q.c-panda.q: Giant pandas live in the wild in which country?
q.c-pizza.e: The art of the Neapolitan pizzaiuolo was inscribed by UNESCO in 2017.
q.c-pizza.q: Neapolitan pizza comes from which Italian city?
q.c-reef.e: It stretches over 2,300 km along the coast of Queensland — the world’s largest coral reef system.
q.c-reef.q: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of which Australian state?
q.c-sauna.e: The sauna is central to Finnish life; Finnish sauna culture is on UNESCO’s intangible heritage list.
q.c-sauna.q: Which country is estimated to have over 3 million saunas for about 5.6 million people?
q.c-tango.e: Tango emerged in the late 19th century in Buenos Aires and Montevideo.
q.c-tango.q: The tango dance originated in the Río de la Plata region shared by Argentina and…?
q.g-alps-highest.e: Mont Blanc, on the France–Italy border, is about 4,806 m high.
q.g-alps-highest.q: What is the highest mountain in the Alps?
q.g-amazon.e: The Amazon has by far the largest discharge of any river — more than the next several rivers combined.
q.g-amazon.q: Which river carries the most water into the sea?
q.g-andes.e: The Andes run about 7,000 km along the western side of South America.
q.g-andes.q: What is the longest continental mountain range in the world?
q.g-atlantic.e: The Atlantic Ocean separates the Americas from Europe and Africa.
q.g-atlantic.q: Which ocean lies between Europe and North America?
q.g-australia-cap.e: Canberra was purpose-built as the capital as a compromise between rivals Sydney and Melbourne.
q.g-australia-cap.q: What is the capital of Australia?
q.g-baikal.e: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, is the deepest lake on Earth (about 1,640 m).
q.g-baikal.q: Lake Baikal, the world’s deepest lake, is in which country?
q.g-brazil-cap.e: Brasília, a planned city, replaced Rio de Janeiro as capital in 1960.
q.g-brazil-cap.q: Brazil moved its capital in 1960. Which city became the new capital?
q.g-canada-cap.e: Ottawa, in Ontario, was chosen as capital by Queen Victoria in 1857.
q.g-canada-cap.q: What is the capital of Canada?
q.g-danube.e: The Danube passes through four national capitals — more than any other river.
q.g-danube.q: Which river flows through Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade?
q.g-deadsea.e: The Dead Sea shore lies around 430 m below sea level, and it is still dropping.
q.g-deadsea.q: The shore of the Dead Sea is the lowest land on Earth. Roughly how far below sea level is it?
q.g-equator-ecuador.e: “Ecuador” is Spanish for “equator”, which crosses the country just north of Quito.
q.g-equator-ecuador.q: Which country is named after the equator?
q.g-everest.e: Everest straddles the border between Nepal and the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
q.g-everest.q: Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and which other country?
q.g-gibraltar.e: At its narrowest it is only about 13 km between Spain and Morocco.
q.g-gibraltar.q: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Europe from which continent?
q.g-greenland.e: Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.
q.g-greenland.q: Greenland, the world’s largest island, is an autonomous territory of which country?
q.g-iceland.e: Iceland straddles the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where the Eurasian and North American plates pull apart.
q.g-iceland.q: Iceland sits on the boundary between which two tectonic plates?
q.g-istanbul.e: The Bosphorus separates European Istanbul from its Asian side.
q.g-istanbul.q: Istanbul is split between two continents. Which strait divides it?
q.g-lesotho.e: Lesotho is an enclave inside South Africa. Eswatini also borders Mozambique.
q.g-lesotho.q: Which country is entirely surrounded by South Africa?
q.g-nile.e: The Nile ends in a large delta in northern Egypt and empties into the Mediterranean.
q.g-nile.q: Into which sea does the Nile flow?
q.g-pacific.e: The Pacific covers about a third of Earth’s surface — more than all the land combined.
q.g-pacific.q: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
q.g-panama.e: The Panama Canal, opened in 1914, lets ships avoid sailing around South America.
q.g-panama.q: Which canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific oceans?
q.g-russia.e: Russia spans 11 time zones and about 17.1 million km².
q.g-russia.q: What is the largest country in the world by area?
q.g-sahara.e: The Sahara is the largest hot desert; Antarctica and the Arctic are larger, but they are cold deserts.
q.g-sahara.q: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
q.g-suez.e: Opened in 1869, the Suez Canal crosses Egypt to connect the Mediterranean and the Red Sea.
q.g-suez.q: The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean Sea with which sea?
q.g-timezones-fr.e: Thanks to overseas territories from the Pacific to the Indian Ocean, France uses 12 time zones (13 including its Antarctic claim).
q.g-timezones-fr.q: Counting its overseas territories, which country uses the most time zones?
q.g-turkey-cap.e: Ankara has been the capital since 1923; Istanbul is the largest city.
q.g-turkey-cap.q: What is the capital of Turkey?
q.g-vatican.e: Vatican City covers about 0.49 km² and is entirely surrounded by Rome.
q.g-vatican.q: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
q.h-bastille.e: The Bastille prison was stormed on 14 July 1789, a key event of the French Revolution.
q.h-bastille.q: France’s national day (14 July) commemorates the storming of which fortress?
q.h-berlinwall.e: The border crossings opened on 9 November 1989; Germany reunified in 1990.
q.h-berlinwall.q: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
q.h-greatwall-space.e: False — it is far too narrow. Astronauts confirm it is not visible from the Moon, and barely (if at all) from low orbit.
q.h-greatwall-space.q: True or false: the Great Wall of China is easily visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
q.h-incas.e: Cusco, in today’s Peru, was the Inca capital until the Spanish conquest.
q.h-incas.q: What was the capital of the Inca Empire?
q.h-machu.e: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel in the Peruvian Andes.
q.h-magellan.e: Magellan died in the Philippines in 1521; Juan Sebastián Elcano completed the voyage in 1522.
q.h-magellan.q: Which expedition completed the first circumnavigation of the Earth, in 1522?
q.h-moon.e: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969; Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the surface.
q.h-moon.q: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
q.h-napoleon.e: True — he was born in Ajaccio, Corsica, in 1769, a year after France acquired the island.
q.h-napoleon.q: True or false: Napoleon Bonaparte was born on the island of Corsica.
q.h-pompeii.e: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius in 79 AD buried Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash.
q.h-pompeii.q: Which volcano buried Pompeii in 79 AD?
q.h-silkroad.e: For centuries it connected China with Central Asia, Persia, the Middle East and the Mediterranean.
q.h-silkroad.q: The Silk Road trade network mainly linked China with which region?
q.h-vikings.e: Norse sagas and the site at L’Anse aux Meadows (Newfoundland) support Leif Erikson’s voyage.
q.h-vikings.q: Around the year 1000, which Viking explorer is believed to have reached North America?
q.t-blackbox.e: True — flight recorders are bright orange so they are easier to find after an accident.
q.t-blackbox.q: True or false: an aircraft “black box” flight recorder is usually painted bright orange.
q.t-chunnel.e: Opened in 1994, it runs about 50 km between Folkestone and Coquelles near Calais.
q.t-chunnel.q: The Channel Tunnel connects England with which country?
q.t-concorde.e: Concorde was an Anglo-French project, in commercial service from 1976 to 2003.
q.t-concorde.q: Which two countries jointly developed the supersonic airliner Concorde?
q.t-glacier.e: It links Zermatt and St. Moritz, crossing the Oberalp Pass.
q.t-glacier.q: The Glacier Express is a famous scenic train in which country?
q.t-greatcircle.e: The shortest path on a sphere is a great-circle arc, which appears curved on most flat projections.
q.t-greatcircle.q: Why do long-haul flights look curved on a flat map?
q.t-iata.e: IATA airport codes have three letters; ICAO codes, used by pilots and controllers, have four.
q.t-iata.q: How many letters are in an IATA airport code such as CDG or JFK?
q.t-jetstream.e: The jet stream blows from west to east at altitude, giving eastbound flights a strong tailwind.
q.t-jetstream.q: Why are eastbound flights across the North Atlantic usually shorter than westbound ones?
q.t-left.e: Japan drives on the left, like the UK, Australia, India and many other countries.
q.t-left.q: In which of these countries do people drive on the LEFT side of the road?
q.t-orient.e: The Orient Express became famous for its route between Paris and Constantinople (Istanbul).
q.t-orient.q: The original Orient Express (1883) ran from Paris towards which city?
q.t-route66.e: Route 66 ran about 3,940 km from Chicago to Santa Monica, California.
q.t-route66.q: Historic US Route 66 ran from Chicago to which city?
q.t-shinkansen.e: Japan’s Tōkaidō Shinkansen opened in 1964, just before the Tokyo Olympics.
q.t-shinkansen.q: Which country opened the world’s first high-speed rail line, in 1964?
q.t-transsib.e: At about 9,289 km, it is the longest railway line in the world.
q.t-transsib.q: The Trans-Siberian Railway links Moscow with which Pacific port?
q.t-underground.e: London’s Metropolitan Railway opened in January 1863 using steam locomotives.
q.t-underground.q: Which city opened the world’s first underground railway, in 1863?
q.t-wright.e: Their first flights took place at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, on 17 December 1903.
q.t-wright.q: In which country did the Wright brothers make the first powered flight in 1903?
q.tf-africa-countries.e: True — Africa has 54 UN member states, more than any other continent.
q.tf-africa-countries.q: True or false: Africa has more countries than any other continent.
q.tf-australia-continent.e: True — the Australian continent (Sahul) includes mainland Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea.
q.tf-australia-continent.q: True or false: Australia is both a country and (with nearby islands) a continent.
q.tf-canada-lakes.e: True — Canada has more lakes than any other country; it has hundreds of thousands of lakes.
q.tf-canada-lakes.q: True or false: Canada has more lakes than any other country.
q.tf-equator-brazil.e: True — the Equator crosses northern Brazil, near the mouth of the Amazon.
q.tf-equator-brazil.q: True or false: the Equator passes through Brazil.
q.tf-sahara-rain.e: True — deserts are defined by low precipitation, and Antarctica receives very little.
q.tf-sahara-rain.q: True or false: Antarctica is classified as a desert.
